title: A sent X post never marks its Delivery sent
description:
Found 2026-11-22 on Machines on Machines: both live X posts left their Delivery at sending with attempt 1 started, though X charged for each. The announce agent hands the attempt to Caducus and reads back queued; the site's X function posts it later; nothing read Caducus's record afterwards (XRunner.settle existed but nothing called it). Effects: the Announcements list shows a sent post as sending / Outcome unknown, no result URL is kept, and the settings page's post count for the cycle reads 0 (PPY-8037b8).

Fix: PR #1834. The X function settles the Delivery from Caducus's record right after the post (announcements/settle_after_post.py), with getDelivery and updateDelivery granted to its role; a repeated queue message settles again and never posts twice. After release, the two Deliveries already sent on Machines on Machines need a one-time settle through the operator lane.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A post the X function makes leaves its Delivery sent, with the post id.
- A repeated queue message posts once.
- The two existing Machines on Machines Deliveries read sent.

**Gherkin:** attempt-event-id.feature (the site's X function posts a queued attempt and the Delivery is marked sent; the same message twice posts once).

comments.author: ryan
comments.text: Released in Papyrus 5.146.1 (#1834) and live on Machines on Machines (Amplify job 154). Verified in production: the site's X function, given the queue message of each post already sent, read Caducus's record and closed attempt 1 sent with its own role (getDelivery/updateDelivery); nothing posted again. Both Deliveries now read sent (posts 2124246414221865158 and 2124532286666199213). Open question noted, not filed: the broadcast function's 'delivery' read returns null for the same event ids that the X function and a local run find, so the runner's own immediate read after hand-over sees no record; it does no harm (a repeat is a duplicate) and the X function settles.
